sentences.text: This is an application seeking quashing of the First Information Report in Crime No. 374/2023 registered with Pundalik Nagar Police Station, District Aurangabad for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 r/w. 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Pundalik Nagar Police Station, District Aurangabad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. At the inception, the learned APP for the State objected to the maintainability of this application on the ground of lack of territorial jurisdiction.
He would submit that the offence has been registered with Pundalik Nagar Police Station, District Aurangabad therefore, the application ought to have been filed before the appropriate Bench.

entities.text: Pundalik Nagar Police Station, District Aurangabad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In other words, he would submit that in view of the Chapter 31 of the Bombay High Court Appellate Side Rules, 1960 the RR Jaiswal 2 913-apl-1455-23.odt application is not maintainable as it does not fall in the said criteria.

entities.text: Bombay High Court Appellate Side Rules, 1960
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Shri Vaishnav, learned counsel for the applicants responded by stating that the entire cause of Vijay Vasantrao Manekar And Others vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso, Ps Pundlik Nagar, ...

sentences.text:
on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107071207/
1 action arose within the territorial limits of this Bench.

The applicant nos. 1 and 2 (parents-in-law)
are permanent resident of Nagpur while applicant no. 3 (sister-in-law) is admittedly staying in Indore (Madhya Pradesh).
He would submit that after the marriage, though the informant was earlier staying at Aurangabad, started co-habiting at her matrimonial house at Nagpur.
It is his contention that the entire FIR alleges the instances of so called harassment occurred at Nagpur only.

It is his submission that even not a part of cause of action arose within the territorial limits of concerned Police Station at Aurangabad and therefore, this Court has very much jurisdiction to entertain the application.

To substantiate his contention, he relied on the decision of Supreme Court in the case of Navinchandra N. Majithia Vs. State of Maharashtra [(2000) 7 SCC 640].
5.

entities.text: Navinchandra N. Majithia Vs. State of Maharashtra [(2000) 7 SCC 640]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On fact, the learned counsel for the applicants submits that the allegations are totally false.
He has produced certain documents to falsify allegations levelled therein.
6. We have gone through the Police report from which prima facie it is evident that the allegations pertains to the happening at Nagpur and Pune.
However, we did not find any allegations, meaning thereby, part of cause of RR Jaiswal 3 913-apl-1455-23.odt action within the territorial limits/jurisdiction of Aurangabad Bench.
7. In view of the said factual aspect, we deem it appropriate to issue notice by keeping the point of jurisdiction open.

8. Issue notice to the non-applicants, returnable on 30.11.2023.
9.
The learned APP waives service of notice for non-applicant no. 1/State.
10. In the meantime, the investigation may go on but, charge-sheet shall not be filed without obtaining leave of the Court.
(M. W. CHANDWANI, J.) (VINAY JOSHI, J.) Signed by: Mr. Rajnesh Jaiswal
